The only way to expose the bug is to create a scenario where: (1) the wrong max causes intermediate overflow/underflow that changes relative ratios, OR (2) values are in a narrow range where small max errors produce distinguishable relative differences before normalization. rounds.recommendations: For parallel reduction kernels, mutation testing should verify with narrow-range floating-point values (all within ~1-2 orders of magnitude) where small errors in reduction produce detectable output differences, rather than extreme values where softmax normalization masks the bug.

    # Critical positions that stress specific reduction paths

    # Thread 160 -> s=128 -> thread 32 -> s=64 -> thread 0 (via s=32)
    # Thread 224 -> s=128 -> thread 96 -> s=64 -> thread 32 -> s=32 -> thread 0
    critical_positions_per_row = [
        192,  # warp 6 -> warp 2 -> warp 0
        160,  # warp 5 -> warp 1 -> warp 0
        224,  # warp 7 -> warp 3 -> warp 0
        176,  # warp 5 -> warp 1 -> warp 0
        192,
        208,  # warp 6 -> warp 2 -> warp 0
        240,  # warp 7 -> warp 3 -> warp 1 -> warp 0
        144,  # warp 4 -> warp 1 -> warp 0
        192,

        168,  # warp 5 -> warp 1 -> warp 0
